thread:
leo: Heads up — ran into a weird scoping bug when running the sampleapp in CI. It sent requests against the wrong project.

priya: which project did it use?

leo: our internal `acme-staging` but the CI intent was `acme-experiments`. We set env as:
```
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=rwd_live_abc123
export REDWOOD_PROJECT=acme-experiments
```
but the requests all hit `acme-staging`.

emily: how are you instantiating the SDK? any explicit project arg?

leo: no, using default client: `const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })` and relying on REDWOOD_PROJECT env.

priya: hmm. SDK currently derives project from: 1) explicit constructor opt, 2) env REDWOOD_PROJECT, 3) token-scoped fallback. It should have honored REDWOOD_PROJECT.

leo: digging in logs — SDK logged: `Using project from token: acme-staging (token scope)` which suggests the token has project-level scope baked in and wins over env var.

emily: that's a design choice we made earlier to avoid env var mismatch but it's surprising if token wins silently. Especially for CI jobs where tokens are org-scoped but people try to override to test.

leo: also saw this: when we rotated the key via CLI in the same runner, the SDK continued to use the older key for ~90s and returned intermittent 401s until the process restart.

priya: that indicates the SDK caches the key at init and the CLI rotation path publishes new credentials to `~/.redwood/credentials` but doesn't inform already-running processes.

emily: two issues then: env-var/token precedence surprising, and rotation propagation poor. Suggested fixes?

leo: proposal: make precedence explicit and documented: constructor arg > CLI flags > REDWOOD_PROJECT env > token scope fallback, but add a feature where if REDWOOD_API_KEY env changes we pick it up (with a short polling interval) OR expose a signal handler `/usr/bin/kill -HUP` to reload creds in long-lived processes.

priya: I like explicit precedence. But auto-polling env is scary for varying security surfaces. Maybe only poll if `REDWOOD_API_KEY_AUTO_RELOAD=true` is set. Default to no polling.

emily: or better: provide an API `client.reloadCredentials()` that the app can call after rotation. CLI can optionally call a local control socket if present to trigger reload in dev servers. That keeps behavior opt-in.

leo: also suggest failing fast when there's an obvious mismatch: if REDWOOD_PROJECT env is set and token project (if any) differs, warn at startup and include `--force-token` to keep current behaviour. CI should surface a non-zero exit if mismatch and `REDWOOD_PROJECT_STRICT=true` is set.

priya: agree. Add a warning log at info level by default and treat as error when strict mode is enabled.

emily: docs change too: sampleapp README should stop recommending `REDWOOD_PROJECT` as an override in ephemeral CI jobs and instead recommend passing `--project` to the sampleapp CLI or using per-job service accounts scoped to the intended project.

leo: small reproducible: token metadata from auth service: `{"project":"acme-staging","org":"acme"}`. SDK log: `Using project from token: acme-staging`. Env was `acme-experiments`.

priya: who's owning the SDK patch?

emily: I'll take it. Plan: 1) add explicit precedence and warning, 2) add `client.reloadCredentials()` + doc example, 3) add strict mode env behavior for CI. PR with tests and changelog. ETA 3 days.

devx-bot: task RW-DEVEX-1201 created and assigned to emily. Severity: P2. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/508 (draft).

leo: also can we add a `redwood env lint` subcommand to the CLI that checks for common pitfalls (e.g., REDWOOD_API_KEY present in plain text, export lines in Dockerfiles, REDWOOD_PROJECT mismatch with token metadata) so folks can run it in CI?

priya: nice. low-effort check and useful guardrail. Add as a follow-up.

emily: adding tests to sampleapp CI that run `redwood env lint` before deploy. I'll update the sampleapp templates.

leo: thanks. this will avoid a few production surprises.

priya: also ping support/solutions to update runbooks explaining how to debug scope mismatches (how to inspect token metadata via `redwood auth info --json`).

leo: done, filed a quick note for support.

emily: starting the patch now. Will post PR link + canary plan here when ready.
